column1: # The conformance rows drop elaboration owns (CONFORMANCE.md, owner §3.7): each
# row's migrated program in tests/corpus/, and what `sawc drops --dump` gives
# it: `drops N, flags M` over its elaborated dump, or the refusal standing first.
# A count changes only on purpose: review the program's dump, then this line.

column4: each scope kind releases its locals on its own exits, sync and driven alike; a same-scope redefinition releases the binding it replaces at the redefinition, after its initializer, and that binding's scope end drops nothing
a redefinition whose initializer moves the old binding releases nothing for it: its drop at the redefinition is elided, sync and driven alike
each Copy-tier value has one static drop; the copy's retain is glue (§3.8)
a consumed receiver is released field by field, statically; `self = v` drops the old referent whole, through its deinit
every consuming match takes its scrutinee apart, what an arm leaves over dropped as the arm completes; each part's drop is static
each value is dropped once, in reverse declaration order: `o`, which a non-escaping `[move o]` takes, under its take flag
the visited values keep one static drop each; a visitor lends and drops nothing
a by-value closure parameter is dropped once at the body's end, named or not
a parameter moved into a new owner has its drop elided
the escaping and non-escaping bodies drop their parameter alike
the accumulator moves through each call; only its final owner drops it
the migrated file is refused by typecheck first, a migration artifact
a non-escaping closure's environment owns nothing a drop releases
